item.title: Rust Officially Sets Rules for AI Coding: LLM-Written PRs Must Ship Tests, Merges Circuit-Break at 50%
item.description: On August 5, 2026, five Rust teams adopted an LLM usage policy for rust-lang/rust: AI-created code can land in the compiler, but only with disclosure, mandatory tests, and a ban on soundness-critical paths — and if LLM PRs exceed 50% of merges in any 6-week window, a circuit breaker halts them. Full policy breakdown and community debate inside

item.title: One if Made This Rust Filter 4x Slower: The CPU Was Guessing for You
item.description: Filtering 1M floats: why is keeping half the slowest case? I reproduced the HN-top branch-prediction experiment on Windows (i5-12400F, rustc 1.97.1): a branchless rewrite cut the worst case from 5.1ms to 1.5ms (3.4x faster) — and learned when the trick backfires

item.title: Rust 1.97.1 Emergency Fix: A Compiler Miscompilation Has Been Silently Crashing Programs Since 1.87
item.description: Rust 1.97.1 ships an emergency fix for a long-dormant LLVM miscompilation: 1.97.0 changed Option::None's stored tag from 2 to -1, which triggered a trunc nuw mis-optimization on x86/x64, crashing optimized builds with segfaults. Reproduced on Windows, upgrade guide inside

item.title: Debugging Rust in VS Code: A Complete launch.json Guide with Windows Measurements
item.description: Set up Rust debugging in VS Code: rustup's rust-lldb is not applicable to Windows MSVC; configure CodeLLDB and launch.json, then troubleshoot breakpoints.

item.title: Your 8,000-Line Rust Project Made rust-analyzer Index 2.5M Dependency Lines

item.title: Building a B+Tree in Rust: What I Got Wrong Before Getting It Right

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 3): Refactoring Tools into a Skill Registry with Traits
item.description: Part 3 replaces the Part 1 match dispatcher with a Rust trait system: Skill, Registry, DynSkill, schemars-generated JSON Schema, parallel calls, error classification, retries, hooks, and permission gates.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 4): State Machines for Multi-Step Tasks
item.description: Part 4 introduces state machines for multi-step tasks: Node trait, Graph runner, SQLite checkpointing, Interrupt suspend/resume, PermissionMode gates, and NodeHook cross-cutting logic.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 5): Multi-Agent Crews
item.description: Part 5 covers multi-agent collaboration: when to add agents and when not to. The Agent trait, Crew parallel/sequential dispatch, Router, debate protocol, and composing with Part 3's skill registry and Part 4's state machine.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust — Part 2: Structured Prompt Architecture and the Cache Boundary
